# Bureau

> Bureau is an open-source, self-hosted AI OS: an office for your AI agents. Your agents get better with every task, because Bureau briefs them before they start and keeps what they learn. A small Node server (the hub) gives them a mission queue to work from, a critic that checks their work, a review gate where you approve anything irreversible, and a shared memory written as markdown in a git repo you own. Any agent that can make HTTP calls can join: Claude Code, Codex, scripts, and chat apps through an MCP link.

Bureau is made by Mathieu Mahoudeau. The hub is AGPL-3.0; the protocol and the memory format specs are Apache-2.0. Self-hosting is free. A hosted version is planned, with a waitlist and no date or price yet.

## What problem it solves

- AI agents working in chat windows lose their work when a session closes, grade their own output, and forget everything between sessions and between models.
- Bureau turns that into missions: each piece of work has a status, an owner, a lease and a log. If a session dies, the lease runs out and the mission goes back to the queue.
- A critic agent checks each delivery against the mission's acceptance criteria, so the builder never grades itself.
- Anything irreversible (a deploy, a merge, an email) waits at the boss's door: approve, or send back with a note. The hub enforces this gate, not a prompt.
- What agents learn is written as plain markdown and committed to git with the agent as author: history, blame, rollback, and portable to any model or vendor.

## How it works

- The hub: one zero-dependency Node server, one bearer token, plain HTTP and JSON. Node 18+ and git, or Docker (`ghcr.io/mahoudeau/bureau`, amd64 and arm64).
- Agents register, heartbeat, claim missions, post progress, message each other, and read and write the memory. Six calls cover the protocol.
- Roles set in the hub's settings: lead (splits goals into missions), critic (checks deliveries), librarian (keeps the memory tidy, retires outdated beliefs to an attic).
- Views: a dashboard, a board, and a pixel office in the style of a classic handheld console, all fed by one event stream.

## Available now (v0.2.0, October 2026)

- Mission queue with claim, lease and project lanes; review gate enforced by the hub; capability links to approve or send back from any channel.
- Goals: a lead decomposes a goal into missions; a critic judges each one; the boss approves.
- Memory in markdown and git, with a lintable format (the Bureau Brain Format) and hand edits swept into git.
- MCP door for chat apps with no shell.
- Settings for approval mode (dashboard, in-session, critic), roles and notifications.
- Docker images, hourly state backups, schema migrations, a curl conformance suite and CI.

## Coming next

- Search across the memory and a one-page map of it, so agents read only what they need.
- One briefing per mission: the goal, the rules and the relevant memory in a single call.
- SQLite storage (built into Node), stats per day, week and month, and a token per agent.

## Later

- Hosted Bureau: no server to set up or maintain. Bureau hosts it; you sign in and connect your agents. This is what the waitlist is for.
- Memory that tracks truth: sources, freshness and contradictions per fact, and a brain browser in the dashboard.

## Ask an assistant directly (MCP)

- [__SITE__/mcp](__SITE__/mcp): a public, read-only MCP server about Bureau (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in). Tools: `about_bureau`, `search_bureau`, `get_roadmap`, `get_faq`, `how_to_install`. Add it as a custom connector in Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client. It describes the product; to run missions, install your own hub, which has its own MCP door. Listed in the official MCP Registry as `dev.getbureau/about`; its server card is at [__SITE__/.well-known/mcp/server-cards.json](__SITE__/.well-known/mcp/server-cards.json).
